column1: # Examples transcribed from the postal authorities' free public guides, for the last group of Tier 2 countries (Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Hungary, Romania, Mexico, Australia).

# id <TAB> citation <TAB> country hint <TAB> country line (1 = the example prints it, so the test renders it) <TAB> input (a backslash-n is a line break) <TAB> expected Postal rendering <TAB> expected Display rendering (= when not pinned)

# The input is the guide's example as printed. The Postal expectation is the guide's own text except where noted: the sheets print POLSKA / POLAND and CZECH REP. on the country line and Postal prints the English name of the country; Polish postcodes are written with a hyphen;

# Czech and Slovak postcodes are followed by two spaces (UPU Czech Republic and Slovakia sheets); the Polish, Czech and Slovak post offices print mixed case in their examples and capitals for the post office name in their rules (Poczta Polska; Czech Post), and Postal follows the rules;

# Australia Post's street and locality lines are capitals without punctuation, so a period after St is dropped and a street line printed in mixed case is capitals; Poste restante is printed as the Czech and Polish posts write it (the Slovak sheet prints capitals).

# Sources: UPU country sheets (upu.int, addressing unit): Poland 08/2018, Czech Republic 02/2018, Slovakia 01/2013, Slovenia 05/2016, Croatia 05/2014, Hungary 01/2012, Romania 10/2007, Mexico 03/2017, Australia 07/2017; Czech Post address formats (ceskaposta.cz, retrieved 2026-11-05);
# Australia Post, Address Presentation Standards (1999) and Correct Addressing (November 2022).
